headline: Hyperia City hits shelves, first Set 14 invitational goes to EdLorcana, and Inkdark Collector Boosters get details

tldr.text: Set 14, Hyperia City, went on general sale October 23 after prereleases that started October 16. It adds Coco and the new ink drop mechanic, and the release notes change how stacked keywords work and issue errata for Jukebox.

Edmond Chiu (EdLorcana) won the 16-player Quest World Iconic Clash invitational on October 17, the first big look at Set 14 decks. His list was titled "Emerald / Steel", and several of the broadcast matches were Emerald/Steel.

Into the Inkdark (Set 15) preorders are open for a reported February 12, 2027 release. It brings 12-card all-foil Collector Boosters and the serialized Illustrious rarity (23 copies of each card). Collector Boosters will be sold only at select Play Hub stores and Disney locations.
Flash is the first card people are calling broken in the new format. Manifest TCG calls it a new Steel staple, and Reddit says it's overtuned at 2 cost.

meta.text: Before Hyperia City was legal, Amber/Amethyst Midrange led Core Constructed with about 19% of the meta, followed by Amber/Emerald Elinor and Amber/Emerald Songs.

The 16 QWIC lists, reviewed by Lorcana Villain, included Emerald/Sapphire (Lukas Kaupa), three Amber/Emerald Songs builds (Bryan Pereira, Jacob Frank, Joseph Quigley), Amber/Steel Rockstar Stitch (vVonderland), two Emerald/Amethyst Retro builds (Alessandro Cavalli, Fungus) and Amethyst/Steel. Emerald/Steel showed up in many of the broadcast matches.
Emerald/Amethyst Retro looks like one of the top Set 14 decks: Xenulous (Team Maelstrom) went over how to play against it on JBaum's Alter Academy and shared a decklist.

Ruby/Emerald is the deck everyone's testing: Podcana built 15 Hyperia City decks and asked whether it's real, and a Reddit Ruby/Emerald actions list is getting attention. The Lore College says Amber/Ruby got an upgrade.
Creators keep naming the same new cards as the strongest: Flash (Steel), Max Goof and an Ariel legendary. The Lore College has posted a full Hyperia City tier list.

players.text: Edmond Chiu (EdLorcana) won the Quest World Iconic Clash, a 16-player invitational where the prize was the iconic Hades – Looking for a Deal.

Round 1 QWIC matchups included three-time champion Frank Karsten vs Shane Downey in an Emerald/Steel mirror, Sky (North American Championship runner-up) vs R_M_B, Fungus vs Ace 103, vVonderland vs Bryan Pereira, Lukas Kaupa vs Carl Go Boom, and Mo Shamblin vs Pandemonium Heart.
Darian won the 79-player Through The Decades CCQ Infinity 5K in the US on October 24.
TT_Egelim won Heroes Ink in Germany (36 players), and MatheusCebolas won the 41-player Mont Set Championship in Brazil on October 17.

news.text: Hyperia City release notes: stacked keywords now work differently, "ink drop" has a glossary entry, and Jukebox gets errata so its printed text matches how it actually plays.
Collector Boosters for Into the Inkdark: 12 cards per pack, all foil, with better odds at Enchanted and Iconic pulls. Standard boosters stay the same. A new Inkdark card was also revealed this week.

Upcoming events: a Core Constructed qualifier with a $5K main event in Louisville on October 24–25 (Hyperia City not legal), and Asia's first Disney Lorcana Challenge in Osaka October 30–November 1. DLC Tampa tickets are on sale, and the Cauldron Cup CCQ survey closes October 30.
Ravensburger is rereleasing the D23 2026 boxes and the foil Pooh playmat through an EQL raffle, with separate US and EU entries.
Pixelborn Connect now runs in the browser at pixelborn.app. It has ranked webcam games and a hide-your-hand option for streamers.

community.text: Supply depends a lot on where you are. US players report Hyperia City at or below MSRP and urge people not to overpay, but a Dutch player can only find €75 troves, and one LGS is holding stock back to see how the market develops.

One player asked how to report an LGS to Ravensburger, saying the store resells all its sealed product and promos on the secondary market and fakes event results. Another thread complains that two boxes had matching common-slot sequences and no Enchanteds.
ICL Season 4 Round 6 (Infinity Week) streamed ETB vs Triad and World Class Cards vs Manifest. Decklists are on inkdecks.

Worth a listen: Rules of Villainy ep. 119 goes through the early meta using Brennan DeCandio's decks. Team Descent was on Let's Talk Lorcana for Hyperia hype, and Lorcana Goons' Meta Watch covers the QWIC lists.
